records.title: Automated tactile sensing
records.bibliography: L. D. Harmon, International Journal of Robotics Research 1(2), 3–32, 1982.
records.read_scope: Publisher metadata and exposed footnotes; full article unavailable. Not treated as a full-text or abstract review.
records.finding: An early review establishing the historical depth of automated tactile sensing. No quantitative sensor result from this article is adopted here.
records.limitation: Published material reflects information acquired before January 1981; historical recommendations are not current component specifications.
records.plan_action: Use only as historical background. Set limb requirements from the actual contact tasks and acceptance tests, rather than invoking human-equivalence targets from an unread historical review.
records.novelty: Broad tactile sensing cannot be claimed as a new concept.
records.bibliographic_note: Publisher gives pages 3–32; Cheng bibliography/user transcription gives 3–31. DOI 10.1177/027836498200100201.

records.title: E-skin: From humanoids to humans
records.bibliography: R. Dahiya, Proceedings of the IEEE 107(2), 247–252, 2019.
records.read_scope: Accepted manuscript: introduction and sections comparing electronic-skin requirements, integration routes and flexible/printed electronics; not every concluding paragraph or cited work.
records.finding: The viewpoint contrasts conventional components on flexible substrates with printed and ultrathin electronics. More discrete functionality competes with conformability; requirements depend on the application.
records.limitation: A perspective article is not evidence that a particular printed film has acceptable fatigue life, manufacturing yield, cost or multimodal accuracy.
records.plan_action: Keep a small number of proven modalities in the first product. Put packaged electronics on mechanically supported islands; qualify the complete interconnect and cover. Track area, installed mass and repair time separately from sensor-element thickness.
records.novelty: Flexible multimodal skin and distributed electronics were already established research directions.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1109/JPROC.2018.2890729; repository manuscript is a primary author source.

records.title: Tactile sensing—From humans to humanoids
records.bibliography: R. S. Dahiya, G. Metta, M. Valle and G. Sandini, IEEE Transactions on Robotics 26(1), 1–20, 2010.
records.read_scope: Indexed author/project PDF excerpts: classification figure 2, section III physiology, encoding and regional sensing requirements. Direct PDF retrieval failed; author-uploaded proof excerpts also located.
records.finding: The review distinguishes cutaneous from joint/force sensing, fingertip arrays from large-area skin, and slowly adapting from rapidly adapting tactile channels. Receptor density and required temporal/spatial performance differ by body site.
records.limitation: Biological receptor counts and perceptual acuity do not directly specify electronic taxel pitch, ADC resolution or required robot bandwidth. This is a review, not validation of our sensor stack.
records.plan_action: Preserve held-contact state alongside onset/change events. Specify coarse arm/leg contact localization independently from fingertip dexterity; retain joint encoders and actuator feedback. Test a sustained load so baseline adaptation cannot erase a real contact.
records.novelty: Biomimetic layering and biological data reduction are prior art.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1109/TRO.2009.2033627; author proof: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/220032969_Tactile_Sensing-From_Humans_to_Humanoids

records.title: Directions toward effective utilization of tactile skin: A review
records.bibliography: R. S. Dahiya et al., IEEE Sensors Journal 13(11), 4121–4138, 2013.
records.read_scope: Glasgow institutional abstract and bibliographic record; TUM institutional abstract. Full original text not read.
records.finding: The authors frame useful tactile skin as a system problem involving distributed coverage, simultaneous contacts, acquisition, calibration and real-time interpretation.
records.limitation: The abstract supplies no verified circuit values, experimental operating envelope or manufacturing economics.
records.plan_action: Keep an acceptance matrix spanning material, acquisition, communication, body coordinates and application. A working single taxel cannot close the multi-contact, coverage or latency requirements.
records.novelty: System-level integration, distributed control and calibration are longstanding research topics.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1109/JSEN.2013.2279056. TUM corroboration: https://portal.fis.tum.de/en/publications/directions-toward-effective-utilization-of-tactile-skin-a-review/

records.title: Proximity sensing in robot manipulator motion planning: System and implementation issues
records.bibliography: E. Cheung and V. J. Lumelsky, IEEE Transactions on Robotics and Automation 5(6), 740–751, 1989.
records.read_scope: Author-hosted manuscript: system architecture/local planning, approximately manuscript pages 2–4; author project page identifying the publication. Not all experiments.
records.finding: The tested infrared arrangement provides a roughly 10–15 cm obstacle-detection envelope around the arm and coordinates sensing with about 50 commanded positions per second. Motion is constrained by the sensed free envelope.
records.limitation: The collision-avoidance argument depends on coverage, robot velocities, sensor characteristics and control timing; it is not a guarantee for arbitrary robots or objects.
records.plan_action: Do not describe our pressure-only skin as detecting obstacles before touch. If proximity is added, validate every joint pose and object reflectance/angle against the actual stopping envelope and measured latency.
records.novelty: Distributed sensitive-arm obstacle avoidance predates the proposed product by decades.
records.bibliographic_note: Author source identifies this file with the 1989 publication despite its IEEE 88 filename; project page https://www.edcheung.com/job/sbr/sbr.html.

records.title: Sensitive skin
records.bibliography: V. J. Lumelsky, M. S. Shur and S. Wagner, IEEE Sensors Journal 1(1), 41–51, 2001.
records.read_scope: Original article via MIT teaching archive: introduction; hardware/device requirements and low-cost-process discussion, printed pp.46–47. Other portions not exhaustively read.
records.finding: The paper explicitly links local processing, simple sensing structures, fault tolerance, repairability and manufacture. It discusses rigid active islands joined by flexible interconnects and warns that large-area signal paths collect noise.
records.limitation: The manufacturing costs and forecasts are historical; they cannot be imported into a 2026 BOM. Proposed future millions-of-sensors systems are not demonstrated production yield.
records.plan_action: Keep analog runs short, digitize regionally, provide failed-channel reporting, and cost scrap/rework and replacement operations. Compare complete installed harnesses rather than copper mass alone.
records.novelty: Low-cost, fault-tolerant, distributed artificial skin is an old objective; differentiation must be measured in implementation.

records.title: Conformable, flexible, large-area networks of pressure and thermal sensors with organic transistor active matrixes
records.read_scope: Open primary main text, fabrication and pressure/thermal experiments, figures 1–5 captions; not supplementary data or independent replication.
records.finding: A 12×12 network with 4 mm pitch combines pressure and thermal layers. Net geometry permits 25% extension; larger extension breaks strut wiring. The reported 2, 000 cycles at 20% concern simplified gold test structures, not complete skin. Organic circuitry uses −20/−40 V biases.
records.limitation: The combined thermal demonstration and transistor protection do not establish long-term humidity, abrasion or joint-fatigue performance of a commercial laminate.
records.plan_action: Use the established layered idea with simpler low-voltage electronics, but test heat paths and full-assembly strain independently. Do not substitute conductor-coupon fatigue for connector, adhesive, sensor and wear-cover fatigue.
records.novelty: Pressure-plus-temperature laminated skin is explicit prior art from 2005.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1073/pnas.0502392102. Full paper read through the substantive main experiments; no claim to have visually inspected all images.

records.title: Artificial Skin in Robotics: A Comprehensive Interface for System-Environment Interaction
records.bibliography: M. Strohmayr, doctoral dissertation, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, 2012.
records.read_scope: Selected thesis text: design tradeoffs in chapter 3; chapter 4.1 test procedures, printed pp.152–159; conclusions. Not the complete 217-page PDF.
records.finding: The thesis separates sensitivity and collision protection and evaluates the sensor with its electronics. Its proposed testing includes static indentation, repeatability, dynamic impact, recovery and overload; filtering affects sensitivity and reaction time.
records.limitation: These proposed evaluation procedures are not a universal certification standard. The thesis itself identifies unresolved performance tradeoffs.
records.plan_action: Add controlled dynamic indentation with an independent load/time reference, overload recovery and identical deployed filter settings. The thin TPU wear film is not an impact-energy absorber. Measure seam and mounted-curvature behavior, not flat coupons alone.
records.novelty: Combining mechanical protection with sensing is established; a quantified thin, serviceable implementation can still differentiate.
records.bibliographic_note: KIT title above is fuller than Cheng’s shortened “Artificial skin for robots.” DOI 10.5445/IR/1000028782.

records.title: Conformable and scalable tactile sensor skin for curved surfaces
records.bibliography: Y. Ohmura, Y. Kuniyoshi and A. Nagakubo, ICRA 2006, 1348–1353.
records.read_scope: Original six-page article: abstract, requirements, sections III–IV and beginning of V, figure captions 1–10. Remaining experiment/conclusion paragraphs not exhaustively read.
records.finding: The implementation places 32 photo-reflector sensing elements and a microcontroller on a cut/fold flexible substrate. Optical emitters are time-shared to control power; local SMBus connects to an in-body ring network. Bus capacitance constrains scaling.
records.limitation: Address-space capacity is not simultaneous full-skin throughput. The reported bare-sheet mass excludes subsequently added foam and the complete installed network. Foldability does not imply repeated stretchability.
records.plan_action: Use a small panel family and controlled mechanical relief. Measure aggregate power at the actual scan duty cycle, installed mass, and complete-frame freshness at maximum node count. Retain compact local analog wiring and a robust regional digital link.
records.novelty: Local scanning, reduced wiring, conformable modules and cut-to-shape skin were demonstrated in 2006.

records.title: Development of the tactile sensor system of a human-interactive robot RI-MAN
records.bibliography: T. Mukai, M. Onishi, T. Odashima, S. Hirano and Z. Luo, IEEE Transactions on Robotics 24(2), 505–512, 2008.
records.read_scope: Indexed original first-page abstract/introduction from Georgia Tech repository. PDF download returned 403; main experiments not read.
records.finding: The original abstract reports an integrated soft areal tactile system on RI-MAN and a human-dummy lifting demonstration. No numerical sensor accuracy or robustness result from the full article is adopted here.
records.limitation: Demonstrating a complete robot handling a dummy does not isolate sensor contribution or validate the proposed resistive panel. Semiconductive-pressure-sensor construction described in other reviews is secondary evidence only.
records.plan_action: Use a supported, low-mass test object for initial arm/body contact experiments. Document independently what skin detection contributes, what robot actuation contributes, and what protection is provided mechanically.
records.novelty: Large-area soft robot skin for physical assistance is established prior art.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1109/TRO.2008.917006; publisher article 4458232. Related open chapters were not substituted for this original.

records.title: ARMAR-III: An integrated humanoid platform for sensory-motor control
records.bibliography: T. Asfour et al., IEEE-RAS Humanoid Robots, 2006, 169–175.
records.read_scope: Original article sections on arm sensing and artificial skin, pp.2–3 of PDF, and hierarchical architecture/figure 5. Not all platform experiments.
records.finding: Shoulder and arm skin is integrated through dedicated controllers into CAN, alongside separate joint-torque and wrist force/torque sensors. The architecture separates task planning, coordination and execution.
records.limitation: This platform paper does not provide a standalone production recipe or prove that coarse skin replaces accurate joint or wrist sensing.
records.plan_action: Expose timestamped contact, location, confidence and faults through a dedicated driver. Leave actuator regulation in the existing robot control layer; test timeout handling at every boundary.
records.novelty: CAN-connected local skin processing and whole-robot integration were already present in 2006.

records.title: Design of human symbiotic robot TWENDY-ONE
records.bibliography: H. Iwata and S. Sugano, ICRA 2009, 580–586.
records.read_scope: Author-institution publication record and abstract. Original seven-page article not accessed.
records.finding: The design combines passive arm mechanisms and mechanical softness in joints and skin, derived from a set of assistance-task requirements.
records.limitation: The abstract does not expose contact-force limits, hazard validation, individual skin accuracy or a component-level manufacturing cost.
records.plan_action: Specify service tasks before adding modalities. Verify joint range, friction, cable pull and sensor prestress on a limb fixture; sensing alone cannot make an otherwise stiff mechanism mechanically compliant.
records.novelty: Soft covering combined with passive joint mechanisms is prior art.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1109/ROBOT.2009.5152702. Related Japanese 2008 appearance-design paper is a distinct publication.

records.title: Humanoid robot which can lift a 30 kg box by whole body contact and tactile feedback
records.bibliography: Y. Ohmura and Y. Kuniyoshi, IROS 2007, 1136–1141.
records.read_scope: Author laboratory bibliography and publisher record link verified. Original article unavailable; secondary syndicated abstract seen but not used as verified experimental evidence.
records.finding: The article identity/title documents an early whole-body-contact and tactile-feedback claim. The 30 kg result is a title-level reported claim here, not an audited replication.
records.limitation: No verified gains, failure statistics, force distribution or safety conditions from the original are available in this review.
records.plan_action: Cite the precedent without importing its payload. For our proof, compare skin-enabled and disabled behavior on the same restrained, low-energy fixture with objective contact-detection and response metrics.
records.novelty: Whole-body tactile lifting is not a new application concept.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1109/IROS.2007.4399592; publisher https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/4399592 requires JavaScript verification.

records.title: Whole body haptics for augmented humanoid task capabilities
records.bibliography: Y. Kuniyoshi, Y. Ohmura and A. Nagakubo, Robotics Research, Springer Tracts in Advanced Robotics 66, 61–73.
records.read_scope: Publisher abstract, chapter metadata and references; subscription full chapter unavailable.
records.finding: The abstract reports whole-body tactile covering of an adult-size humanoid and contact-motion experiments including a 66 kg human dummy.
records.limitation: The abstract alone cannot validate the loading conditions, control robustness or economics. It cannot justify human-lifting demonstrations with a home-lab prototype.
records.plan_action: Keep the early demonstrator on arms and legs, with bounded low-load contact tasks and no human support. Explain the eventual application without implying its hardware/control validation is already complete.
records.novelty: Whole-body contact capability and human-like distributed haptics are established motivations.
records.bibliographic_note: Publisher citation/copyright says 2010; Cheng/user list says 2011 and lab bibliography also lists the 2011 book. Keep this edition/year discrepancy visible. DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-14743-2_6.

records.title: An embedded artificial skin for humanoid robots
records.bibliography: G. Cannata, M. Maggiali, G. Metta and G. Sandini, MFI 2008, 434–438.
records.read_scope: Entire substantive five-page original article, including architecture, transducer, microcontroller, experiments and conclusions; figure captions. Images not independently resolved.
records.finding: Twelve capacitive taxels per triangle use AD7147 conversion; up to 16 triangles/192 taxels connect through local buses to one MCU/CAN. A grounded deformable electrode enables contact from insulating objects and shielding. About 500 Hz averaged sensing trades spatial detail for speed; individual channels are slower.
records.limitation: The reported prototype is six triangles, with quantitative experiments ongoing. Three-to-five-millimeter foam differs from our thin laminate. Port count does not imply adaptive rerouting.
records.plan_action: Keep local aggregation and distinguish normal-force sensing from bare capacitive human-touch detection. If evaluating capacitive alternatives, include the full ground-electrode, dielectric and cover stack and measure both spatial detail and response time.
records.novelty: Modularity, local conversion, CAN aggregation and adaptive spatial resolution are prior art.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1109/MFI.2008.4648033. Extracted area/power units in early PDF are ambiguous; no power-density number is adopted.

records.title: Methods and technologies for the implementation of large-scale robot tactile sensors
records.bibliography: A. Schmitz et al., IEEE Transactions on Robotics 27(3), 389–400, 2011.
records.read_scope: Author-uploaded manuscript: sections I, III, V and VI-A–D, assembly figure captions. Not every hysteresis equation or grasping trial.
records.finding: The 16-bit CDC yielded 8 usable signal bits in that assembly. Drift adaptation freezes while touched. Probe geometry changes response, and some body configurations omit a top electrode and rely on a human ground plane.
records.limitation: The extracted drift pseudocode has an apparent missing minus sign versus its stated ±0.5 deadband; never copy it blindly. Published sensor performance does not transfer to our resistive laminate.
records.plan_action: Freeze baseline during contact; test slow ramps and sustained loads. Measure actual noise-limited resolution. Test plastic, metal and gloved contacts. Calibrate several probe diameters and mounted curvature rather than claiming pressure accuracy from one probe.
records.novelty: Cheap replaceable COTS-based skin with distributed buses and calibration is prior art.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1109/TRO.2011.2132930. Uploader is coauthor Marco Maggiali; original author-site URL currently 404.

records.title: A flexible and robust large scale capacitive tactile system for robots
records.bibliography: P. Maiolino, M. Maggiali, G. Cannata, G. Metta and L. Natale, IEEE Sensors Journal 13(10), 3910–3917, 2013.
records.read_scope: Author manuscript sections III–IV, integration text and experimental figure captions; most main text read, not supplementary data.
records.finding: The design uses clothing-industry 3D spacer fabric and removable covers. On the flat 2 mm dielectric prototype, 15 load cycles with one-minute rests gave a maximum 9.1 fF cycle difference at 28.6 kPa, roughly 5% of range. Pressure-insensitive reference capacitors compensate structural thermal drift; they are not surface thermometers. The reported acquisition operates at 25 Hz.
records.limitation: Ten-minute constant-displacement relaxation is not a constant-force creep or lifetime test. Neither its thickness nor performance transfers to a 1.5 mm 100 Hzresistive stack.
records.plan_action: Use this as a capacitive fallback benchmark, subject to full-stack comparison. Separate thermal-point sensing from pressure compensation. Test both constant-force and constant-displacement holds plus local heating while loaded.
records.novelty: Fabric-based, protected, serviceable robot skin predates this proposal.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1109/JSEN.2013.2258149. arXiv submission 2014 is an author copy of the 2013 article.

records.title: A new silicone structure for uSkin—A soft, distributed, digital 3-axis skin sensor and its integration on humanoid robot iCub
records.bibliography: T. P. Tomo et al., IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 3(3), 2584–2591, 2018.
records.read_scope: Indexed primary accepted manuscript section III-A/B, tableI and figure 1–2 captions; direct repository PDF retrieval failed. Calibration/results not fully read.
records.finding: Sixteen magnetic 3-axis cells occupy 26×27×6.05 mm; approximately 1 mm mounting tape adds thickness. Bumps and air gaps reduce normal-to-shear mechanical coupling. A first soft-silicone attempt allowed magnets to attract each other.
records.limitation: Full assembly is thicker and more complex than a thin resistive film. Performance in motor magnetic fields, chosen cover adhesives and our limb geometry remains unverified.
records.plan_action: Reserve this modality for a shear-sensing variant. If evaluated, test magnetic interference with motors energized, overload, cross-axis coupling and mounting-tape creep; include every protective/mounting layer in thickness and cost.
records.novelty: Soft protected digital 3-axis skin is already demonstrated; simplified normal-contact coverage targets a different specification.
records.bibliographic_note: Use the accepted 2018 manuscript as the source; no unverified calibration accuracy or DOI is invented.

records.title: An adjustable force sensitive sensor with an electromagnet for a soft, distributed, digital 3-axis skin sensor
records.bibliography: A. C. Holgado et al., IROS 2018, 2582–2588.
records.read_scope: Author-institution abstract and publication identity; original full text not read.
records.finding: The prototype replaces a permanent magnet with an electromagnet so current can change force sensitivity in a soft magnetic sensor.
records.limitation: The abstract does not establish a mass-production cost or justify extra power, thermal coupling and calibration for approximate normal-pressure sensing.
records.plan_action: Exclude electromagnets from the baseline. Add them only if a specified force-range problem cannot be met passively and a measured benefit exceeds coil-power, heat and driver cost.
records.novelty: Electronically adjustable magnetic tactile sensitivity is prior art.

records.title: A real-time distributed architecture for large-scale tactile sensing
records.authors: E. Baglini, S. Youssefi, F. Mastrogiovanni and G. Cannata
records.read_scope: Official IROS2014 digest, p.134, and author-uploaded abstract; original seven-page paper not obtained.
records.finding: Describes an EtherCAT-based distributed network connecting computational nodes associated with skin patches and evaluates the real-time architecture.
records.limitation: The accessible material does not establish the exact hardware cost, measured deadline distribution, or fault containment available to this project. EtherCAT results cannot certify a CAN FD implementation.
records.plan_action: Adapt its separation of local acquisition, transport and host processing. Keep CAN FD for the low-cost baseline; qualify deadlines under maximum traffic before increasing node count.
records.test: Timestamp ADC scan completion, CAN transmission, gateway reception and consumer execution separately. Test every region at maximum active traffic while logging, displaying data and injecting node resets.
records.novelty: Distributed patch processing and real-time tactile networking are established prior art.

records.title: A real-time data acquisition and processing framework for large-scale robot skin
records.authors: S. Youssefi, S. Denei, F. Mastrogiovanni and G. Cannata
records.read_scope: Publisher-indexed introduction and selected architecture/implementation sections, including Skinware abstraction and historical test platform. Full results and figures not reviewed.
records.finding: Skinware separates tactile applications from particular sensors and network technologies and treats data coherence, consistency and timing as architectural concerns. Its reported environment includes RTAI and an older Linux platform.
records.limitation: Historical software-platform results do not establish present ROS2/Linux deadline behavior or direct STM32/CAN compatibility.
records.plan_action: Adopt immutable complete-scan snapshots with versioned metadata and bounded producer-consumer queues. Keep real-time consumers independent from visualization, file I/O and discovery.
records.test: Freeze or crash the UI/logger while exercising acquisition. Assert the control consumer sees either a coherent fresh snapshot or an explicit invalid/stale state, never a mixture of scans.
records.novelty: A common sensor abstraction and real-time skin middleware are established; contribution must be reproducible integration quality and cost.

records.title: Asynchronous, event-driven readout of POSFET devices for tactile sensing
records.authors: S. Caviglia, M. Valle and C. Bartolozzi
records.read_scope: Identity and conference pages2648–2651 checked against ISCAS proceedings contents; original abstract/body not obtained. DOI corroborated by later scholarly reference lists.
records.finding: The title establishes an earlier POSFET/event-readout line of work. No device-level performance or circuit claim from this paper is relied upon here.
records.limitation: No original circuit schematic, process, power, noise or bandwidth was available for audit; a POSFET circuit cannot be presumed equivalent to the chosen resistive film.
records.plan_action: Do not transplant or cost a POSFET circuit from this citation. The baseline continues to use a conventional ADC and firmware change detection; identify that as sampled event reporting.
records.test: Document actual scan period and first-sample latency. Do not label the MCU design a continuously asynchronous transducer.
records.novelty: The title is enough to flag asynchronous tactile readout as pre-existing work; performance comparison requires the original paper.

records.title: Event-driven encoding of off-the-shelf tactile sensors for compression and latency optimisation for robotic skin
records.authors: C. Bartolozzi et al.
records.read_scope: Author-uploaded manuscript excerpts: architecture, encoding comparison and conclusions. Primary IIT laboratory publication listing also checked. Full paper was not independently downloaded.
records.finding: Studies event encodings of existing tactile sensors, including recorded iCub fingertip data, and describes an FPGA-based acquisition path with hierarchical event addressing. Sensor conversion and event transport are distinct stages.
records.limitation: Fingertip datasets, FPGA acquisition and AS-AER links do not demonstrate whole-limb resistive-film performance. Encoding simulations and hardware properties must be distinguished.
records.plan_action: Adopt explicit body/patch/site identifiers, acquisition timestamps and a reproducible raw-data-versus-event comparison. Keep CAN integrity and periodic absolute snapshots; reject an FPGA hub as the minimum-cost baseline.
records.test: Replay identical raw recordings through periodic and hybrid encoders. Report event onset misses, absolute reconstruction error, bytes on the wire and end-to-end age, including packet overhead.
records.novelty: Off-the-shelf tactile event conversion, address hierarchies and event compression are prior art.

records.title: The event-driven software library for YARP—With algorithms and iCub applications
records.authors: A. Glover, V. Vasco, M. Iacono and C. Bartolozzi
records.read_scope: Publisher-indexed sections3.2–3.3 on event representation, readers/queues and processing; complete article body not retrieved.
records.finding: Provides event packet representations and software handling in YARP, with processing decoupled from receipt. The discussion recognizes large variations in event traffic and computation.
records.limitation: Its illustrative large-rate examples concern vision. A flexible event library does not establish a hard skin-control deadline or justify silently skipping required control updates.
records.plan_action: Adapt recording/replay, typed event records and independent receive/processing threads. Use bounded queues with counters and an explicit overload state; make GUI frame dropping independent of tactile validity.
records.test: Burst all sites simultaneously, pause each consumer, then resume. Verify bounded memory, monotonically sequenced records and deterministic stale-data handling.
records.novelty: Event middleware and replay are established infrastructure; do not market them as a new sensory nervous system.

records.title: Reactive motion control for human-robot tactile interaction
records.bibliography: T. Wosch and W. Feiten, ICRA 2002, pp. 3807–3812.
records.read_scope: Citation identity checked against DBLP; a ResearchGate-hosted abstract was found, but no primary full text or primary abstract was successfully retrieved. The secondary abstract is not used as implementation evidence.
records.finding: The bibliographic record establishes tactile interaction control as a research subject by 2002; no equation, response rate or robustness result is verified here.
records.limitation: The controller's assumptions, saturation handling and experimental limits cannot be audited from the accessed material.
records.plan_action: Retain as historical related work only. Implement our contact-to-response state machine from explicitly specified requirements and better-accessed sources [63,64,82], not this inaccessible paper.
records.novelty: Do not claim invention of tactile robot interaction; this record is evidence of earlier work, not a legal assessment of claims.

records.title: Real-time collision avoidance in teleoperated whole-sensitive robot arm manipulators
records.bibliography: V. J. Lumelsky and E. Cheung, IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics 23(1), 1993, pp. 194–203.
records.read_scope: NASA repository abstract and metadata. Author-hosted TR91.pdf was identified as an earlier technical report, not silently treated as the exact 1993 journal article.
records.finding: The abstract describes combining operator commands with whole-arm sensing for reactive obstacle avoidance in teleoperation.
records.limitation: The original proof conditions, sensor range and timing are not available in the abstract. Contact-only resistive film cannot supply pre-contact distance.
records.plan_action: Document pre-contact detection as an external robot capability. Bench demonstrations may report contact detection and subsequent response; they must not label the film a collision-prevention sensor.
records.novelty: Whole-arm awareness and reactive avoidance have substantial prior art.

records.title: Whole-arm reactive collision avoidance control of kinematically redundant manipulators
records.bibliography: C. L. Boddy and J. D. Taylor, ICRA 1993, vol. 3, pp. 382–387.
records.read_scope: DBLP identity and secondary Science Explorer abstract located. No author/publisher full text retrieved; secondary abstract is excluded as technical proof.
records.finding: Citation confirms an early whole-arm reactive-control contribution. Its mathematical or experimental guarantees were not verified.
records.limitation: Insufficient evidence to reproduce the controller or infer performance on the proposed robot.
records.plan_action: Our design must explicitly handle infeasible withdrawal: abort the application task and request the platform's validated stop/hold rather than promise a retreat direction for every contact configuration.
records.novelty: Redundancy-based whole-arm reaction is not a day-one novelty claim.

records.title: Programming by touch: The different way of human-robot interaction
records.bibliography: G. Grunwald, G. Schreiber, A. Albu-Schaffer and G. Hirzinger, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics 50(4), 2003, pp. 659–666.
records.read_scope: DLR publication record; repository explicitly does not supply the full text. No algorithm inferred from the title.
records.finding: Bibliographic prior art for programming robots by physical interaction.
records.limitation: No controller parameters, sensor specifications or validation details were inspected.
records.plan_action: Treat teaching as an explicit operator-enabled mode. Record start, stop, allowed body zones and sampled robot trajectory independently from autonomous operation. Cite this paper only for historical positioning until its original text is available.
records.novelty: Touch teaching itself is established prior art.

records.title: Manual guidance for industrial robot programming
records.bibliography: D. Massa, M. Callegari and C. Cristalli, Industrial Robot 42(5), 2015, pp. 457–465; DOI 10.1108/IR-11-2014-0413.
records.read_scope: University repository metadata and complete abstract; no attached full text available.
records.finding: The abstract describes manual robot programming using a force/torque sensor and demonstrates an industrial application.
records.limitation: Force/torque sensing is not equivalent to an uncalibrated normal-contact film. Exact control gains, task constraints and failure behavior remain unverified.
records.plan_action: Measure teaching time, operator interventions and replay error in a controlled benchmark. Use the robot's supported hand-guiding function when available; do not substitute skin intensity for a specified six-axis sensor.
records.novelty: The contribution must be reduced installed sensing/maintenance cost, not manual guidance as a new application.

records.title: Tactile sensing in intelligent robotic manipulation—A review
records.bibliography: J. Tegin and J. Wikander, Industrial Robot 32(1), 64–70, 2005.
records.read_scope: Author-uploaded text: introduction, sections 5.2–5.7 and conclusions. KTH thesis reprint located but oversized PDF could not be retrieved.
records.finding: The review separates distributed contact sensing from intrinsic force/torque sensing. It discusses mechanical inversion through soft covers, FSR/capacitive drift and hysteresis, and the loss of contact-pattern information in few-wire analog schemes.
records.limitation: Its supplier listings and dimensions are historical. A single resultant force/position cannot identify an arbitrary set of simultaneous contacts.
records.plan_action: Preserve separate taxel identities for multi-contact limb sensing. Do not infer shear, friction, material hardness or accurate force from ordinal normal readings without additional measurement and a validated model.
records.novelty: Resistive arrays, capacitance sensing, local processing and few-wire tactile tradeoffs are established.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1108/01439910510573318; uploader identified as author Johan Tegin.

records.title: Sensitive manipulation: Manipulation through tactile feedback
records.bibliography: E. Torres-Jara and L. Natale, International Journal of Humanoid Robotics 15(1), 1850012, 2018.
records.read_scope: Author manuscript abstract/introduction, hardware figure 1 and sections 4.1.3–4.3, PDFpp.12–15. Not all experiments.
records.finding: Obrero combines compliant actuation with tactile strategies for acquiring and maintaining contact. The text explicitly notes missed contacts at unsensed joint regions and a lift/retry strategy when immediate slip sensing is inadequate.
records.limitation: Success depends on hand hardware, force control and exploration strategies absent from our coarse arm/leg panels. It does not show that simply adding taxels delivers dexterity.
records.plan_action: Include unsensed joint seams in coverage maps. Demonstrate one bounded contact-aware behavior and compare against a baseline, recording missed contacts; do not claim general slip detection or dexterous grasping.
records.novelty: Tactile-first manipulation and active contact exploration are prior art.
records.bibliographic_note: Accepted manuscript datedOctober 2017 for the 2018 publication.

records.title: High-density conformable tactile sensing glove
records.bibliography: T. Sagisaka et al., IEEE-RAS Humanoids 2011, 537–542.
records.read_scope: Author laboratory bibliography verified; original full text not accessed. Exact-paper syndicated abstract and a distinct 2012 JRSJarticle abstract were seen, and are not substituted for the original.
records.finding: An established high-density sensing-glove research line. Original-paper performance numbers are not independently verified in this record.
records.limitation: Bibliographic aggregators merge the 2011 conference and 2012 Japanese journal article. Their results must not be silently treated as the same document.
records.plan_action: For our arm/leg application, evaluate range-of-motion change, cable pull and pressure offsets with the covering installed. Tree/branch geometry is a useful candidate, but requires complete laminate fatigue testing.
records.novelty: High-density conformable sensing and joint-motion-aware routing are prior art, not a new conceptual claim.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1109/Humanoids.2011.6100898. Related primary 2012 paper: https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jrsj/30/7/30_30_711/_article/-char/en (DOI 10.7210/jrsj.30.711).

records.title: Development and applications of high-density tactile sensing glove
records.bibliography: T. Sagisaka, Y. Ohmura, A. Nagakubo, K. Ozaki and Y. Kuniyoshi, EuroHaptics 2012, LNCS 7282, 445–456.
records.read_scope: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record; subscription chapter not read in full.
records.finding: The abstract describes 1, 052 pressure sites per hand using 1 mm elements on FPC, and human experiments relating pressure distribution to external-force direction and exploratory behavior.
records.limitation: Correlation in a human-worn glove does not establish calibrated robot shear-force measurement, full-body fatigue or inexpensive manufacturing.
records.plan_action: Keep human-dexterity claims out of the limb-panel proof. If comparing density, state active area, sensor-element size and pitch separately, with installed mass and connectivity included.
records.novelty: Thousands of tactile channels with flexible routing were already demonstrated in human sensing equipment.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-31401-8_40. Different publication from[32].

records.title: Tactile object class and internal state recognition for mobile manipulation
records.bibliography: S. Chitta, M. Piccoli and J. Sturm, ICRA 2010, 2342–2348.
records.read_scope: Indexed author-hosted original conference PDF methods/results excerpts, especially tablesII–IV. Direct PDF retrieval timed out; later journal version was kept distinct.
records.finding: At 20 N probing, reported container-class accuracy is 93.9%, while internal-state accuracy varies substantially by container (water bottles 32.5%). Stronger probing improves one container result, illustrating task and stimulus dependence.
records.limitation: An overall recognition number cannot be transferred across object types or contact forces; high probing forces can damage objects. These are controlled gripper observations, not generic limb-skin intelligence.
records.plan_action: For any classifier, report per-class confusion matrices and separate test objects/sessions from training. Keep active exploratory-force tests outside the baseline ordinal-contact product unless actuator force is independently measured.
records.novelty: Tactile object/state classification is prior art; any claimed advantage needs a matched task benchmark.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1109/ROBOT.2010.5509923. Do not substitute chitta 10 tro.pdf journal expansion for this conference paper.

records.title: Learning inverse dynamics models with contacts
records.bibliography: R. Calandra, S. Ivaldi, M. P. Deisenroth, E. Rueckert and J. Peters, ICRA 2015, pp. 3186–3191; DOI 10.1109/ICRA.2015.7139638.
records.read_scope: Author PDF, 6 pages; abstract, §§II–III, §IV-A through E and conclusion read. Filename says 2016; bibliographic paper is 2015.
records.finding: Mixtures of Gaussian-process contact experts predict torque residuals. In §III-A, tactile data select contacts; proximal force/torque readings supply force information. Experiments use additional calibrated joint-torque sensors as targets. The multiple-contact experiment is sequential contact at alternate obstacles.
records.limitation: This does not establish torque learning from the proposed film alone or arbitrary simultaneous-contact generalization. Ground-truth sensor calibration and training coverage matter.
records.plan_action: Keep learned dynamics outside the first control path. An optional offline comparison must log synchronized encoders, skin, reference F/T and torque targets, and split training/test by physical trial and unseen pose/contact condition.
records.novelty: Learning contact dynamics from skin is prior art; a new contribution needs a fair independent benchmark.

records.title: A simple tactile sensing foot for humanoid robot and active ground slope recognition
records.bibliography: K. Suwanratchatamanee, M. Matsumoto and S. Hashimoto, IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics, 2009, 1–6.
records.read_scope: Publisher abstract and introduction excerpt, not the complete sensor/control evaluation.
records.finding: The work uses a small set of thin force-sensitive resistors and active foot interaction to classify ground slope rather than requiring a dense whole-foot image.
records.limitation: A foot-slope demonstration does not validate arm/leg pressure sensing or balance stability. Its load paths and contact geometry differ from shell-mounted skin.
records.plan_action: Keep feet as a separate subsystem. Establish whether a future task needs contact presence, center of pressure, slope or detailed pressure distribution before selecting sensor count.
records.novelty: Task-specific sparse sensing and active haptic inference are established.

records.title: Design and experiment of the NAO humanoid robot’s plantar tactile sensor for surface classification
records.bibliography: Q. Yuan and J. Wang, ICISCE 2017, 931–935.
records.read_scope: Author-uploaded original: abstract, sections III–Vthrough classifier setup, diagrams/captions. Final result table and conclusion not exhaustively read.
records.finding: A 10×16 resistive array uses 400 samples/s acquisition, but the authors explicitly state 0.4 s per full image; a 20-site subset supports faster tracking. Classification aggregates multiple walking steps.
records.limitation: The text’s 360 total datasets versus 224 training+36 test is arithmetically inconsistent. The headline accuracy is not immediate response or demonstrated cross-robot generalization. Matrix bypass-current rejection is not established by the viewed block diagram.
records.plan_action: Publish ADC rate, per-taxel rate, full-frame rate, scan skew and reaction latency separately. Never borrow 400 Hz as a full-array benchmark. Retain independent sensing islands unless simultaneous-contact electrical crosstalk is experimentally bounded.
records.novelty: Low-cost resistive skin plus simple classification is prior art.
records.bibliographic_note: DOI 10.1109/ICISCE.2017.197. Uploader is coauthor Jianxiao Wang; no outreach performed.

records.title: An adaptive sensor foot for a bipedal and quadrupedal robot
records.bibliography: K. Fondahl et al., BioRob 2012; Cheng lists 270–275.
records.read_scope: DFKI institutional publication abstract and metadata. Original paper not read.
records.finding: The work concerns an adaptive foot mechanism and its sensor integration for different legged platforms, rather than simply applying a sensing film to an unchanged foot.
records.limitation: The abstract is insufficient to reproduce mechanics, control or load qualification. The institutional page’s pagination conflicts with Cheng’s bibliography.
records.plan_action: Do not roll feet into the limb-panel BOM. A foot version needs its own contact mechanics, abrasion, overload, water/soil and gait-interface requirements.
records.novelty: Adaptive sensorized feet are an established separate product/problem class.
records.bibliographic_note: DFKI displays 2780–2786 whereas Cheng and other citations show 270–275. Flag the discrepancy; do not silently choose unverified metadata.

records.title: A ZMP sensor for a biped robot
records.bibliography: M. Shimojo, T. Araki, A. Ming and M. Ishikawa, ICRA 2006, 1200–1205.
records.read_scope: Indexed author-hosted first-page abstract. Direct PDF retrieval 403; complete derivation and experiments not read.
records.finding: The abstract reports four wires, response within 1 ms, 0.2 g/cm²areal mass, and simultaneous total load and center-of-load position.
records.limitation: These are compressed aggregate outputs, not independent contact locations.0.2 g/cm²equals 2 kg/m²; “lightweight” must be compared using consistent units. No claim about general dynamic ZMP equivalence is adopted.
records.plan_action: Test observability before replacing arrays: two equal separated contacts and one central contact can share a centroid. Our multi-contact requirement needs independent sites or another demonstrated reconstruction method.
records.novelty: Extreme wire reduction with analog spatial aggregation is prior art; it trades away information.

records.title: High-speed pressure sensor grid for humanoid robot foot
records.bibliography: Y. Takahashi, K. Nishiwaki, S. Kagami, H. Mizoguchi and H. Inoue, IROS 2005, 3909–3914.
records.read_scope: Author-institution abstract and bibliographic record. Original six-page paper not accessed.
records.finding: The abstract reports a 32×32 matrix, 1 kHz sampling, 14-bit conversion and 0.6 mm force-sensitive rubber. It explicitly identifies bypass-current interference and a mitigation method.
records.limitation: The abstract cannot supply the exact mitigation circuit or demonstrate our laminate’s independence, accuracy or fatigue. ADC resolution is not mechanical force accuracy.
records.plan_action: Our 100 Hzbody panels should not be marketed as equivalent to high-speed sole sensing. Any cheaper shared resistive matrix must pass a multi-contact test including unselected-row leakage, not merely isolated single presses.
records.novelty: Dense, thin resistive tactile arrays and scanning-crosstalk remedies are well-established research.

records.title: Humanoid multimodal tactile-sensing modules
records.authors: P. Mittendorfer and G. Cheng
records.read_scope: University bibliographic record and abstract; full methods, circuit and characterization tables not obtained.
records.finding: Describes modular off-the-shelf multimodal skin with local digitization/processing and network connectivity, including temperature, acceleration and proximity sensing.
records.limitation: This earlier hardware generation should not be conflated with the later force-cap version. Its multimodal capability is absent from a pressure-plus-NTC patch.
records.plan_action: Adopt local processing and replaceable modules. Publish an explicit modality table: approximate normal contact and two temperature points in baseline; no shear, proximity or inertial self-localization.
records.test: For every advertised modality, demonstrate a repeatable stimulus, calibration, uncertainty and fault response using the actual production-intent patch.
records.novelty: Modular multimodal cells and local intelligence existed by2011.

records.title: Integrating discrete force cells into multi-modal artificial skin
records.authors: P. Mittendorfer and G. Cheng
records.read_scope: Repository-indexed first-page abstract, force-cell construction and introduction. Full force/displacement graphs and durability results not reviewed.
records.finding: Uses etched CuBe2 spring structures with capacitive measurement, three force cells per skin module, and automated assembly concepts. The paper reports2.5kHz acquisition filtered to250Hz and SNR greater than50dB.
records.limitation: These figures belong to a metal-spring capacitive transducer, not a printed resistive taxel. Encapsulation and mechanical preload affect performance. CuBe processing is not proposed for the home-lab film route.
records.plan_action: Adopt mechanical overload stops, controlled preload and a cover-specific calibration record. Reject copying its performance numbers or force-cell BOM into the resistive design.
records.test: Calibrate each finished cover/sensor/carrier stack, repeat after remounting and after overload, and measure loading/unloading hysteresis and zero drift.
records.novelty: Protected multimodal force cells and assembly-oriented mechanics are prior art.

records.title: Towards autonomous robotic skin spatial calibration: A framework based on vision and self-touch
records.authors: A. Albini, S. Denei and G. Cannata
records.read_scope: Primary university publication list verifies identity; a secondary abstract describes RGB-D/self-touch, but original abstract/body was not obtained. The secondary <2mm result is deliberately not adopted as validated evidence.
records.finding: This is relevant prior art for spatial calibration using vision and robot-generated contacts; no exact original algorithm or performance claim is used in the design.
records.limitation: Reachability, camera calibration, occlusion and force-distributed contact centroids need examination before reproduction. The source available here is insufficient to promise its accuracy.
records.plan_action: Keep registered CAD carriers as the baseline. Use external probing at marked sites as a measurable manufacturing check; describe any future vision/self-touch implementation as a separate reproduction.
records.test: Blindly probe predeclared site centers in several poses and report position and normal errors against the fixture geometry, rather than only fitting error.
records.novelty: Vision-assisted and self-touch spatial registration are not a new claim for this project.

records.title: 3D surface reconstruction for robotic body parts with artificial skins
records.authors: P. Mittendorfer and G. Cheng
records.read_scope: Repository first-page abstract/introduction and university abstract. The supplied2019 review §II-C supplies additional secondary explanation of reconstruction.
records.finding: Reconstruction uses the modular skin's known structural geometry and motion-related sensing. The approach concerns shaped, connected modules rather than an arbitrary uninstrumented stretchable sheet.
records.limitation: A shared CAN address list does not reveal physical adjacency; resistive touch values do not supply gravity vectors. Stretch and slip violate a fixed module geometry assumption.
records.plan_action: Adopt a versioned body map with per-site position and unit normal derived from the rigid carrier. Bind map revision to the installed carrier and reject unknown revisions.
records.test: Check normals at curved-edge sites as well as patch centers. Remount and probe several positions; inhibit control if the carrier cannot be registered within the declared tolerance.
records.novelty: Automatic surface reconstruction from instrumented skin is existing work, but is not implemented by the baseline BOM.

records.title: Open-loop self-calibration of articulated robots with artificial skins
records.authors: P. Mittendorfer and G. Cheng
records.read_scope: Repository-indexed pages1–2 including algorithms1–2, requirements and experimental/simulation scope; university abstract read directly. Full numerical results not obtained.
records.finding: Uses tri-axis accelerometers and isolated joint excitation to find segment/joint activity and construct kinematic models. Requires instrumented rigid segments and a static reference. Physical KUKA results establish structural exploration; parameter estimation is additionally demonstrated in simulation.
records.limitation: Does not validate autonomous geometry from pressure-only skin. Weak excitation, reference motion and unobserved degrees of freedom can make identification ambiguous. Full numerical error bounds were not inspected.
records.plan_action: Adapt activity-matrix validation using a reusable stationary-reference/downstream IMU fixture and known joint states. Retain CAD geometry; label the fixture an adaptation, not a full reproduction of autonomous skin localization.
records.test: Use one joint at a time; repeat with reversed motion and held-out poses. Compare detected influence with the robot kinematic tree and reject low-SNR or inconsistent results.
records.novelty: Activity matrices, motor excitation and accelerometer-based structural self-calibration are prior art.

records.title: Automatic robot kinematic modeling with a modular artificial skin
records.authors: P. Mittendorfer, E. Dean and G. Cheng
records.read_scope: University abstract and bibliographic record read directly. Original six-page article unavailable. Supplied2019 review §II-D is secondary evidence for axis/SVD/radius sequence.
records.finding: Uses per-cell tri-axis accelerometers, open-loop motions and circle-point analysis to build a forward kinematic model. The abstract reports a physical UR5 experiment on an inertial dual-arm platform.
records.limitation: No original numerical errors, conditioning tests or implementation parameters were accessible. One revolute motion identifies perpendicular radius, not the axial component of a sensor offset; full geometry needs additional constraints.
records.plan_action: Use axis/perpendicular-radius estimation only as an offline cross-check against CAD. Do not claim recovery of every DH offset, mass, inertia or friction from a dual-IMU experiment.
records.test: Fit acceleration versus known angular acceleration, retain confidence intervals and residuals, and validate against independent measured radii and unseen poses. Reject rank-deficient fits.
records.novelty: Automatic kinematic modeling from skin acceleration precedes this project. A low-cost reusable fixture may be an implementation distinction, subject to measurement.
records.bibliographic_note: Humanoids2014 proceedings; university record lists publication12Feb2015. Both dates refer to the same paper.

records.title: 3D spatial self-organization of a modular artificial skin
records.authors: P. Mittendorfer, E. Dean and G. Cheng
records.read_scope: Primary university abstract and identity. Full equations and numerical experiments not obtained.
records.finding: Combines skin-patch geometry with an active LED visual marker and a calibrated monocular camera for spatial registration, including partial visibility.
records.limitation: Self-organization here is not entirely camera-free. A pressure-only film lacks the per-cell inertial and active-marker information of the studied system.
records.plan_action: Maintain a declared manual/CAD root transform. If camera registration is used in a fixture, make camera intrinsics, marker geometry and observation quality part of its calibration record.
records.test: Register from several independent views; probe points withheld from the transform fit and verify the transform direction and units.
records.novelty: Camera-assisted skin registration is prior art; baseline simplicity is a cost/design choice, not a discovery.

records.title: Touch, in Principles of Neural Science, fifth edition, chapter23
records.authors: E. P. Gardner and K. O. Johnson
records.read_scope: User-supplied2019 bibliography identifies chapter23, pp.498–529. Full chapter not obtained; publisher book URL is a locator, not a claim of chapter access.
records.finding: Biological background cited by the2019 review. No receptor count, frequency range or quantitative biological claim is extracted here without the original chapter.
records.limitation: A biological analogy cannot establish robot sensitivity, safety, durability or wiring requirements.
records.plan_action: Describe the design as functionally inspired by distributed sensing. Preserve persistent contact state and temperature measurements; avoid claiming replication of human skin's complete receptor system.
records.test: Maintain a held contact for at least60s and verify it never disappears merely because signal change becomes small. Measure drift separately from valid sustained contact.
records.novelty: Distributed sensing inspired by skin is a long-established concept.

records.title: Touch is a team effort: Interplay of submodalities in cutaneous sensibility
records.authors: H. P. Saal and S. J. Bensmaia
records.read_scope: Original article abstract indexed by PubMed; full review body not obtained.
records.finding: The review emphasizes joint contributions of afferent submodalities to natural touch, rather than a simple one-receptor/one-percept correspondence.
records.limitation: It does not show that two engineered layers or sparse thermal sensors reproduce the capabilities of human skin.
records.plan_action: Keep claims modality-specific. Fuse contact and temperature at the application layer without implying that sparse NTC readings provide a complete thermal image or that normal pressure measures shear.
records.test: Test thermal drift during contact and heat without contact. Report each modality's spatial sampling, temporal response and cross-sensitivity separately.
records.novelty: Biological multimodal integration is motivation, not an invention claim for a pressure/temperature laminate.

records.title: Event-based signaling for reducing required data rates and processing power in a large-scale artificial robotic skin
records.authors: F. Bergner, P. Mittendorfer, E. Dean-Leon and G. Cheng
records.read_scope: Repository-indexed results page6, figures7–8/table/conclusion, plus official conference abstract. Whole methods not retrieved.
records.finding: A260-cell UR5 study reports remaining traffic of16.45% at rest and47.69% under heavy stimulation without timestamps; with timestamps,21.38% and62%. Compact packets of three events suit the correlated modalities studied.
records.limitation: These are remaining-traffic fractions, not reduction percentages. Packet format, timestamps and workload matter. The baseline's64-byte absolute CAN frames will not inherit these reductions.
records.plan_action: Use this as a benchmark design, not a promised percentage. Specify maximum50% idle snapshot-count reduction for100Hzactive/50Hzidle, with smaller total savings after extra overhead.
records.test: Run quiet, motor-moving, stroking, impact and simultaneous-contact workloads. Count complete wire traffic and CPU time, not only useful sensor bytes.
records.novelty: Local send-on-change for large robot skin and compression benchmarks are prior art.

records.title: Event-based signaling for large-scale artificial robotic skin—Realization and performance evaluation
records.authors: F. Bergner, E. Dean-Leon and G. Cheng
records.read_scope: Repository-indexed introduction/architecture and primary university abstract; complete experiment methods not accessed.
records.finding: Uses two260-cell patches with local processing. The abstract reports48.2% packet and17.79% CPU reductions in reactive control; a worst-case5000-cell extrapolation gives21.2% and17.46%, respectively.
records.limitation: The5000-cell result is an extrapolation, not a physical5000-cell validation. Traffic, CPU and control-rate metrics are different quantities.
records.plan_action: Keep a periodic diagnostic mode and a hybrid event mode in the same firmware for controlled comparison. Publish measured patch count and extrapolated counts separately.
records.test: Replay identical captures in both modes with the same host code. Measure CPU, latency, dropped samples and reconstruction error at1,8 and multiple independent regions.
records.novelty: Switchable periodic/event skin operation and performance comparisons were already demonstrated.

records.title: Efficient event-driven reactive control for large scale robot skin
records.authors: F. Bergner, E. Dean-Leon and G. Cheng
records.read_scope: Repository first-page abstract/introduction. Detailed control proofs and full experimental plots not accessed.
records.finding: Evaluates event-driven reactive control on TOMM with two253-cell patches. The abstract reports controller CPU reductions of78% idle and66% during contact relative to the tested synchronous reference.
records.limitation: Controller savings cannot be substituted for network or driver savings. Unchanged pressure does not imply unchanged joint torque when robot configuration changes.
records.plan_action: Cache contact information or link-frame wrench contributions, but recompute their mapping with current joint states in a bounded controller cycle. Separate event receipt from command execution.
records.test: Hold one contact steady while changing joint pose in simulation. Compare event-mode joint torques against a fully recomputed periodic reference, including stale/missing frames.
records.novelty: Event-driven reactive control is prior art; the project's value must lie in verified affordability and integration.

records.title: A128×128120dB15µs latency asynchronous temporal contrast vision sensor
records.authors: P. Lichtsteiner, C. Posch and T. Delbruck
records.read_scope: Original journal-paper reproduction, concluding page575 and indexed abstract. The reproduction is on a secondary host; full article not retrieved.
records.finding: A custom asynchronous contrast imager reports120dB dynamic range,15µs latency and23mW power. Its discussion identifies event-bandwidth limitations and lack of direct DC response.
records.limitation: These are optical custom-silicon results under the paper's conditions. They do not establish response time, energy or resolution for a scanned tactile array.
records.plan_action: Use only as historical distinction between truly asynchronous transduction and100Hz sampled send-on-delta. Retain absolute contact samples so static loads remain observable.
records.test: Measure tactile latency with a stimulus reference and oscilloscope; never infer it from the event-camera title.
records.novelty: Custom event sensors and address-event transmission have decades of prior art.

records.title: An asynchronous time-based image sensor
records.authors: C. Posch, D. Matolin and R. Wohlgenannt
records.read_scope: Primary institutional bibliographic metadata checked. A secondary abstract was found, but no original body or complete primary abstract was reviewed.
records.finding: Identified as prior work on asynchronous time-based optical sensing. No quantitative device claim is adopted.
records.limitation: It is an image-sensor design, not a tactile transducer or low-cost STM32 reference circuit.
records.plan_action: Do not add custom timing-coded hardware to the baseline on this citation alone. Ordinary absolute ADC values plus timestamps are sufficient for the intended touch task.
records.test: Document acquisition instant separately from packet arrival and verify that changing event encoding does not change the underlying sampling limit.
records.novelty: Time-based event representations are established and are not a defensible novel claim here.

records.title: AER EAR: A matched silicon cochlea pair with address event representation interface
records.authors: A. van Schaik and S.-C. Liu
records.read_scope: Primary institutional abstract. This is the2005conference paper, not the later similarly named journal work.
records.finding: Describes paired silicon cochleae, inner-hair-cell/spiking-neuron circuitry and address-event output; its experiment uses tones from different directions.
records.limitation: An auditory analog front end offers no directly transferable tactile resolution, component price or contact-safety guarantee.
records.plan_action: Use it as a historical example of modality-specific local event generation. Keep pressure and temperature acquisition parameters independently specified.
records.test: Verify both modalities retain correct physical units, sampling schedules and invalid-data flags when packed into shared transport.
records.novelty: Neuromorphic sensory event coding predates this project.

records.title: VLSI analogs of neuronal visual processing: A synthesis of form and function
records.authors: M. Mahowald
records.read_scope: Caltech thesis repository metadata and abstract. The full thesis was located but not read.
records.finding: Develops analog VLSI visual processing and communication inspired by neural systems, including retina/stereo/optic-nerve concepts.
records.limitation: A thesis abstract cannot support detailed circuit reproduction or performance comparison. Visual neuromorphic circuitry does not specify the mechanics of electronic skin.
records.plan_action: Cite as historical context if using the artificial-nervous-system analogy. Keep the engineering argument based on tested latency, reliability, mass and cost.
records.test: Audit the article's novelty claims against documented prior art and distinguish implementation economics from a new sensory-computing principle.
records.novelty: Neural-inspired distributed sensing and event communication are longstanding.

records.title: Point-to-point connectivity between neuromorphic chips using address events
records.authors: K. A. Boahen
records.read_scope: Author-hosted abstract and repository-indexed discussion/arbiter figures; not all19journal pages.
records.finding: Analyzes address-event communication and arbitration for time-multiplexed neuromorphic connections. Queueing and contention affect event timing and throughput.
records.limitation: AER timing properties do not remove finite bandwidth, arbitration delay or buffer limits, and do not automatically apply to CAN FD.
records.plan_action: Adopt worst-case burst and queue analysis. Preserve acquisition timestamps and distinguish age at sampling from transport delay; report queue overflow as invalid coverage.
records.test: Align maximum-rate reports from every node and inject retransmissions. Measure worst observed age and overflow behavior, not merely mean latency.
records.novelty: Sparse addresses and asynchronous arbitration are prior art.

records.title: Asynchronous DC-free serial protocol for event-based AER systems
records.authors: P. M. Ros, M. Crepaldi, C. Bartolozzi and D. Demarchi
records.read_scope: Primary university abstract; original article file is restricted and was not requested from authors.
records.finding: Proposes a serial event protocol with100Mbps raw rate and up to2.9million32-bit events/s; its abstract reports successful16-bit operation with ±2% clock mismatch, explicit flow control and AC-coupling compatibility.
records.limitation: These figures refer to that protocol and implementation. A differential pair does not make it electrically or logically interchangeable with CAN.
records.plan_action: Retain CAN FD transceivers, arbitration, error detection and diagnostics. Consider AS-AER only after a measured bandwidth bottleneck justifies separate FPGA/PHY cost.
records.test: Validate the actual CAN line, termination, bit timing and error recovery. Never substitute AS-AER bitrates into the CAN capacity calculation.
records.novelty: Serial event transport over a small wire count is already established.

records.title: A QVGA143dB dynamic range frame-free PWM image sensor with lossless pixel-level video compression and time-domain CDS
records.authors: C. Posch, D. Matolin and R. Wohlgenannt
records.read_scope: IEEE title/record and primary AIT institutional identity; original methods and figures not obtained. Similar2010ISSCC conference versions are not substituted.
records.finding: Identifies prior work on frame-free optical sensing with time-domain encoding; no numerical claim beyond the bibliographic title is adopted as engineering evidence.
records.limitation: The2019 review's use as an example of absolute-value event coding does not make its optical circuit an appropriate tactile design.
records.plan_action: Carry absolute values in the MCU frames; do not integrate received signed increments as the only persistent contact state.
records.test: Drop a contact-onset packet and confirm a subsequent absolute snapshot restores the current state. Also report that the missed transient itself cannot be reconstructed.
records.novelty: Absolute-value/time-coded event sensing is not new.

records.title: A new protocol for a low power sensor network
records.authors: M. Neugebauer and K. Kabitzsch
records.read_scope: Author-uploaded abstract and official conference contents; original protocol details and results not read.
records.finding: Discusses event-oriented activity for battery-powered sensor networks, relating communication scheduling to energy consumption.
records.limitation: Energy benefits depend on the radio, duty cycle and application. A wired sensor that continues sampling at100Hz does not save ADC/MCU power simply because it sends fewer packets.
records.plan_action: Separate bandwidth reduction from power reduction in the cost/performance table. Measure total rail current in both periodic and hybrid modes with identical scan schedules.
records.test: Measure quiet, contact and fault-mode current at the patch input and regional hub; include quiescent regulators and termination/transceiver activity.
records.novelty: Event-based low-power sensor networking was established well before this project.

records.title: Send-on-delta concept: An event-based data reporting strategy
records.authors: M. Miskowicz
records.read_scope: Official MDPI static PDF downloaded locally; all15pages49–63 read, including equations1–13, tables1–2, software example and references. Figure3 on p.58 visually inspected.
records.finding: Separates continuous level-crossing from periodically sampled compound implementations (p.53). Its traffic analysis depends on signal slope, peak density and threshold, and its example compares59 periodic samples with7 events over1.2s at amplitude resolution0.2 (p.58). Heartbeat updates are already described on pp.60–61.
records.limitation: The analytical comparison assumes a specified signal and resolution; it is not a universal saving, hard latency guarantee or loss/reboot protocol. The sample-count example is a simulation, not a tactile-skin experiment.
records.plan_action: Adapt to a hybrid:100Hz scanning, delta/contact/fault triggers and fresh absolute snapshots at least every20ms while idle. Include sequence, reboot/session identity and capture time; never treat silence as healthy.
records.test: Test delta-boundary noise, slow ramps, sustained contacts, burst loss, reboot, timestamp wrap and queue rejection. Keep100Hz worst-case provisioning and measure achieved savings.
records.novelty: Send-on-delta, compound sampled implementations and added heartbeat updates are all established; this project adapts them.

records.title: A robust and efficient dynamic network protocol for a large-scale artificial robotic skin
records.authors: C. Bader, F. Bergner and G. Cheng
records.read_scope: Repository-indexed abstract, first-page introduction and topology/rerouting figure. Detailed implementation and remaining experiments not read.
records.finding: Tests a multi-hop skin network with up to204cells. The original abstract reports recovery within50ms and more than30% packet-loss reduction from balancing relative to its previous protocol.
records.limitation: The supplied2019 review reports40ms and32% greater network size: those are distinct source/metric statements, not interchangeable guarantees. Rerouting requires an intact alternate physical path.
records.plan_action: Reject literal mesh routing on the single shared CAN bus. Use regional segmentation, bounded failure detection and physical fault containment. Any redundancy needs additional buses/ports and its own BOM.
records.test: Unplug a node, break a trunk, short the bus and reset the gateway separately. Record the actual affected region and recovery; do not claim single-wirebreak survival from software alone.
records.novelty: Dynamic robotic-skin routing and load balancing are prior art, but are not functions of the baseline CAN topology.

records.title: Realizing whole-body tactile interactions with a self-organizing, multi-modal artificial skin on a humanoid robot
records.bibliography: P. Mittendorfer, E. Yoshida and G. Cheng, Advanced Robotics 29(1), 2015, pp. 51–67; DOI 10.1080/01691864.2014.952493.
records.read_scope: Author PDF, 17 pages; hardware tables, §§3–4.3, §5, grasping experiments and limitations/conclusion examined. Equations for activity and sensory-motor mapping checked.
records.finding: The calibration assumptions include a fixed reference, rigid links, actuated revolute joints and accelerometer-equipped cells on body parts. Gravity-aligned motion can hide activity; complementary orientations help. HRP-2 uses balance/foot tasks above tactile upper-body behavior, with designated contact zones.
records.limitation: Closed-loop/underactuated structures are outside its stated calibration assumptions. The base low-cost patch lacks the required accelerometers and proximity channel. Incomplete skin coverage can leave forces unobserved.
records.plan_action: Use versioned CAD/manual cell-to-link positions and normals first. A removable IMU jig must have its own repeatability tests; do not advertise automatic arbitrary-sheet reconstruction. Mark coverage gaps and allowed interaction zones explicitly.
records.novelty: Multimodal whole-body tactile behavior and self-organization are established; low-cost serviceable implementation must be differentiated experimentally.

records.title: From multi-modal tactile signals to a compliant control
records.bibliography: E. Dean-Leon, F. Bergner, K. Ramirez-Amaro and G. Cheng, Humanoids 2016, pp. 892–898.
records.read_scope: Author PDF, 7 pages; §§II–III, IV-A and IV-D–F, experimental section and conclusion read.
records.finding: Skin signals become weighted normal virtual forces, then Jacobian-transpose joint commands. The torque resolver includes virtual nonlinear dynamics initialized from measured robot state and inner velocity feedback to limit virtual/real drift. Dynamic-model construction is parametric, not identification of actual masses from geometry alone.
records.limitation: The paper is not a complete deployable controller for an unspecified actuator. Gains, physical/model parameters, tracking behavior, saturation and transport delay still require platform-specific validation.
records.plan_action: Specify command units and robot API explicitly. Never scale torque directly into a position increment. Use an OEM-supported compliance/admittance interface or a separately tested bounded trajectory generator with state feedback, tracking-error limits and reset rules.
records.novelty: A general tactile-to-compliance framework is prior art.

records.title: Whole-body active compliance control for humanoid robots with robot skin
records.bibliography: E. Dean-Leon, J. R. Guadarrama-Olvera, F. Bergner and G. Cheng, ICRA 2019, pp. 5404–5410; DOI 10.1109/ICRA.2019.8793258.
records.read_scope: TUM author-affiliated abstract and metadata; original full paper unavailable. Cheng 2019's summary is secondary evidence, not a substitute full-text read.
records.finding: The abstract describes hierarchical whole-body compliance on a position-controlled humanoid with more than 1,260 skin cells.
records.limitation: The abstract cannot establish reproducible balance constraints, gains, fault response or equivalence with our slower, less multimodal hardware.
records.plan_action: Keep the humanoid's existing balance/stance controller authoritative. Demonstrate the skin on a fixed-base fixture before limb integration; expose contact observations to the OEM whole-body controller rather than directly commanding leg withdrawal.
records.novelty: Thousands of skin cells and whole-body compliance predate this venture.

records.title: TOMM: Tactile omnidirectional mobile manipulator
records.read_scope: TUM publication record and full abstract; original implementation paper not read.
records.finding: The described system combines two six-DOF arms, an omnidirectional wheeled base, exchangeable end effectors and multimodal skin, with integrated hardware/software/middleware.
records.limitation: A wheeled robot integration is not proof of stable bipedal response. Its platform cost and full integration effort cannot be inferred from the abstract.
records.plan_action: Separate skin subsystem BOM from robot, gateway, software integration and tooling. First integration contract must name joint-state rate, command interface, clocks, error states and OEM supervisor ownership.
records.novelty: Multimodal tactile mobile manipulation is an existing application class.

records.title: An overview of null space projections for redundant, torque-controlled robots
records.bibliography: A. Dietrich, C. Ott and A. Albu-Schaffer, International Journal of Robotics Research 34(11), 2015, pp. 1385–1400.
records.read_scope: DLR author manuscript, 17 PDF pages; §2 assumptions, consistency formulations, §4.2 actuator-limited experiment and §§5.1–5.2 discussion read.
records.finding: Torque projection consistency depends on the inverse/weighting choice. Successive projections are not generally a strict hierarchy beyond two tasks. A reported dynamically consistent formulation became unstable when requested torques exceeded actuator limits/bandwidth.
records.limitation: Full-row-rank assumptions and inertia-model errors matter. Algebraic null-space cancellation does not guarantee feasible, stable behavior after saturation or under rank changes.
records.plan_action: Use the existing robot constraint solver. Test conflicting three-task cases, rank loss, actuator limits and task activation/deactivation. Require bounded commands and measured violation metrics; do not declare a weighted sum or naive projector a guaranteed priority controller.
records.novelty: Task hierarchy mathematics is established prior art.

records.title: Synthesis of whole-body behaviors through hierarchical control of behavioral primitives
records.bibliography: L. Sentis and O. Khatib, International Journal of Humanoid Robotics 2(4), 2005, pp. 505–518.
records.read_scope: Author-hosted journal PDF, 14 pages; §§1–4 including equations 17–22, §5 simulated example and discussion read.
records.finding: Constraints, task behavior and posture are prioritized. Projected Jacobian rank indicates whether lower-priority motion remains feasible; an infeasible task can be modified or removed. The presented example is a simulated 24-DOF humanoid.
records.limitation: A mathematical hierarchy under model assumptions is not a certified bound on real contact forces; the physical actuator/network limitations of our robot are unspecified by this paper.
