records.plan_action: Define ordered responsibilities: platform stability and hard limits, collision/contact policy, application trajectory, posture. Log infeasibility and stop/hold decisions. Evaluate conflict cases in simulation before authorizing bounded fixture motion.
records.novelty: Hierarchical combination of balance, contact and manipulation is not novel.

records.title: Efficient distributed torque computation for large scale robot skin
records.bibliography: F. Bergner, E. Dean-Leon and G. Cheng, IROS 2018, pp. 1593–1599; DOI 10.1109/IROS.2018.8594144.
records.read_scope: TUM abstract; original author PDF at mediatum/1459300 returned rate/access errors. Detailed fixed-point/poly approximation description available only through the user-supplied Cheng 2019 review.
records.finding: The abstract proposes moving skin torque computations to distributed electronics to reduce central computation burden.
records.limitation: No audited original implementation, error bound or timing budget. Reduced host computation does not remove network latency, joint-state distribution, stale data or common-mode faults.
records.plan_action: Benchmark host computation and same-link wrench aggregation first. Keep individual contact records for constraints. Introduce MCU-side kinematics only after profiling shows a real bottleneck and synchronization/fault tests pass.
records.novelty: Distributed skin torque computation has explicit prior art.

records.title: Tactile-based whole-body compliance with force propagation for mobile manipulators
records.bibliography: Q. Leboutet, E. Dean-Leon, F. Bergner and G. Cheng, IEEE Transactions on Robotics 35(2), 2019, pp. 330–342; DOI 10.1109/TRO.2018.2889261.
records.read_scope: TUM abstract; primary PDF mediatum/1474210 identified but access failed. Earlier conference paper [77] read separately and not represented as this journal article.
records.finding: The abstract describes constrained, limb-level optimization and propagation of unaccommodated interactions through a mobile robot, experimentally evaluated on a dual-arm platform.
records.limitation: No original full-text audit of constraint values, feasibility conditions or controller failure handling. A mobile-manipulator result does not establish walking-humanoid balance.
records.plan_action: Represent unaccommodated contact as explicit supervisor status. Demand solver deadline, infeasibility, actuator saturation and stop/hold behavior in the robot integration specification; no automatic propagation into biped motion in the baseline.
records.novelty: Force propagation and whole-body compliance are not new features.

records.title: Humanoid robot HRP-2
records.read_scope: Citation identity checked; third-party PDF mirror found but not successfully retrieved. Related AIST platform material is not substituted for the original article.
records.finding: Establishes the identity of the humanoid platform used in later skin demonstrations; no original platform design data are used here.
records.limitation: This bibliography entry does not provide our robot's actuator, balance, thermal or payload specification.
records.plan_action: Require a platform-specific integration sheet, including allowable added mass/inertia by link and supervisor behavior. The skin project must not inherit HRP-2 capability or reconstruct the humanoid from this citation.
records.novelty: Platform provenance only; no skin novelty inferred.

records.title: Integration of robotic technologies for rapidly deployable robots
records.bibliography: E. Dean-Leon et al., IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics 14(4), 2018, pp. 1691–1700; DOI 10.1109/TII.2017.2766096.
records.read_scope: Author PDF contains duplicated proof material (22 pages for an approximately 11-page manuscript); architecture, §V deployment/application results, footnote 13 and conclusion read.
records.finding: The work integrates skin, controls and teaching. It reports installation/calibration of skin on two industrial robots in about five hours. Its functional-safety discussion explicitly identifies a starting point and preliminary productization work.
records.limitation: Installation time is setup-specific, not a promised production takt time. This article does not certify the proposed skin or establish its commercial cost.
records.plan_action: Time assembly, programming, calibration, fitting, remapping and replacement separately. Include integration/service labor in cost comparisons and publish failed/reworked units, not only successful demonstrations.
records.novelty: Rapid deployment is already a research objective; prove a measurable service-time advantage under matched coverage and function.

records.title: A survey of unknown object grasping and our fast grasping algorithm—C shape grasping
records.bibliography: Q. Lei, J. Meijer and M. Wisse, ICCAR 2017, pp. 150–157; DOI 10.1109/ICCAR.2017.7942677.
records.read_scope: TU Delft original conference repository abstract and metadata. Related thesis chapter located but not used as a complete read of the conference paper.
records.finding: The abstract surveys unknown-object grasp methods and describes C-shape grasp selection from partial point clouds, evaluated in simulation.
records.limitation: This is a grasp-planning contribution, not an affordable limb-skin fabrication or calibrated-force result.
records.plan_action: Out of scope for the arm/leg skin prototype. Keep grasp planner and hand sensing as external systems; do not add finger hardware, camera cost or grasp-success claims to the baseline skin deliverable.
records.novelty: Unknown-object grasp planning and tactile-informed grasping both have extensive prior art.

records.title: A unified approach for motion and force control of robot manipulators: The operational space formulation
records.bibliography: O. Khatib, IEEE Journal on Robotics and Automation RA-3(1), 1987, pp. 43–53; DOI 10.1109/JRA.1987.1087068.
records.read_scope: Author-hosted first-page abstract/introduction indexed by search; direct PDF fetch repeatedly timed out. Full equation audit uses [64,68] and the supplied Cheng 2019 text instead.
records.finding: The abstract introduces a task-space dynamic framework for unified motion and force control.
records.limitation: No additional theorem or exact implementation parameter is asserted from this limited read. A Jacobian-transpose mapping is only meaningful with compatible origins, frames and units.
records.plan_action: Unit-test virtual work: f dot (Jv qdot) equals (Jv transpose f) dot qdot. Check moment-origin transformations and distinguish applied environmental wrench from selected reaction command sign.
records.novelty: Operational-space force-to-torque mapping is foundational prior art.

records.title: Robot Control: The Task Function Approach
records.bibliography: C. Samson, B. Espiau and M. Le Borgne, Clarendon/Oxford University Press, 1991; ISBN 9780198538059.
records.read_scope: Bibliographic book metadata; no chapter text retrieved or read.
records.finding: Background reference identity only. No chapter-specific technical claim is made.
records.limitation: The book cannot be treated as an implementation manual actually inspected in this review.
records.plan_action: For each implemented task, define coordinates, error, Jacobian, units, command interface, constraints and termination conditions directly in the project specification; support implemented formulas with the accessible papers.
records.novelty: Task-based robot control is mature background, not a new skin contribution.

records.title: Integration of reactive, torque-based self-collision avoidance into a task hierarchy
records.bibliography: A. Dietrich, T. Wimbock, A. Albu-Schaffer and G. Hirzinger, IEEE Transactions on Robotics 28(6), 2012, pp. 1278–1293; DOI 10.1109/TRO.2012.2208667.
records.read_scope: DLR author manuscript, 15 PDF pages; formulation, damping/task-transition treatment, experiment setup and limitations examined.
records.finding: The method combines repulsive collision tasks with damping and smooth task activation to control torque discontinuities. Experiments use a fast torque-controlled platform; reported controller cycle is 1 ms.
records.limitation: Geometric closest-point changes and interacting repulsive fields complicate behavior. Its actuator interface and timing differ from our 100 Hz skin acquisition.
records.plan_action: Inflate collision geometry by the assembled skin and cable envelope. Test contact enter/leave, changing nearest points and simultaneous contacts; bound command slope and record saturation. Do not equate sample rate with full control bandwidth.
records.novelty: Reactive collision avoidance with smooth hierarchy integration is prior art.

records.title: Tactile-based compliance with hierarchical force propagation for omnidirectional mobile manipulators
records.bibliography: Q. Leboutet, E. Dean-Leon and G. Cheng, Humanoids 2016, pp. 926–931; DOI 10.1109/HUMANOIDS.2016.7803383.
records.read_scope: Author PDF, 6 pages; introduction and §II modeling assumptions, skin-force and propagation formulation read; not a complete experimental replication audit.
records.finding: The modeled mobile base is holonomic with planar translation and yaw. The assumptions explicitly neglect base tilting/instability and upper-limb coupling.
records.limitation: Those omissions are material for humanoid balance and loaded arm interaction. They cannot be carried silently into a biped product.
records.plan_action: Use a fixed base for the proof of concept. Return unresolved contact status to an existing platform supervisor; disable autonomous base/leg response unless a separate model and balance-validation campaign covers it.
records.novelty: Hierarchical propagation of skin interactions is existing research; a cheaper substrate does not supply the omitted dynamics.

records.title: Safe and dependable physical human-robot interaction in anthropic domains: State of the art and challenges
records.bibliography: R. Alami et al., IROS 2006; DOI 10.1109/IROS.2006.6936985.
records.read_scope: Author-hosted workshop manuscript, 15 PDF pages; §§II-A, III-A/B and IV sensor/dependability discussion read. Version/pagination differ from publisher metadata; standards discussion is historical, not current compliance advice.
records.finding: The paper treats physical design, sensing, control, fault handling and maintenance as coupled dependability concerns. A soft cover does not remove the consequences of high effective inertia.
records.limitation: Its 2006 standards and injury-limit discussion are not present-day design limits. The paper supplies no safety qualification of this new film or electronics.
records.plan_action: Inject open, short, stale data, reboot and wrong-map faults in the complete application chain. Verify that operator-visible coverage validity and platform stop/hold state reflect them. Test on an instrumented fixture before human contact experiments.
records.novelty: Mechanics-plus-control dependability is established engineering, not a differentiator by itself.

records.title: Impedance control: An approach to manipulation: Part III—Applications
records.bibliography: N. Hogan, Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement, and Control 107(1), 1985, pp. 17–24.
records.read_scope: MIT-hosted original paper, 8 pages; introduction, impedance selection and obstacle-avoidance derivation read, especially pp. 17–20 and simplifying assumptions.
records.finding: Interaction control specifies a dynamic relationship between motion and force. The illustrative optimization trades interface force against motion error under explicit simplified environmental assumptions.
records.limitation: An illustrative continuous-time optimum does not fix robust digital gains for unknown contact stiffness, transport delay, actuator bandwidth or the nonlinear resistive skin.
records.plan_action: Validate the complete sampled robot/controller/environment loop. Sweep fixture stiffness, delays and load classes; measure oscillation, peak reference force and settling. Do not claim passivity from positive damping alone or compute physical contact power from intensity units.
records.novelty: Impedance/admittance behavior is mature prior art.

records.title: A new actuation approach for human friendly robot design
records.bibliography: M. Zinn, B. Roth, O. Khatib and J. K. Salisbury, International Journal of Robotics Research 23(4–5), 2004, pp. 379–398; DOI 10.1177/0278364904042193.
records.read_scope: Author-hosted journal abstract/first page and one search-indexed §3.1.3 passage on saturation inspected. Direct full PDF fetch failed. Closely titled ISER/ICRA versions are not substituted.
records.finding: The abstract motivates reducing effective impedance while preserving torque performance. The inspected saturation passage explains loss of ideal torque-source behavior when the smaller actuator saturates.
records.limitation: No complete actuation-design or experimental audit; paper-specific performance cannot be assigned to our robot or skin.
records.plan_action: Include reflected inertia, drive friction, limits and braking behavior in the integration contract. Compare added skin/harness mass by link and resulting inertia, not just total grams saved.
records.novelty: Low effective impedance and lightweight actuation are prior art outside this skin subsystem.

records.title: Control of generalized contact motion and force in physical human-robot interaction
records.bibliography: E. Magrini, F. Flacco and A. De Luca, ICRA 2015, pp. 2298–2304; DOI 10.1109/ICRA.2015.7139504.
records.read_scope: Author-hosted abstract/introduction and search-indexed early modeling passages inspected; repeated direct PDF fetches timed out. Classified conservatively because full paper was not retrieved.
records.finding: The inspected text treats contact-point motion/force control using robot dynamics and contact geometry. A contact on an intermediate link has a different Jacobian from the end effector.
records.limitation: No full experimental/equation audit. Normal-only resistive sensing cannot recover arbitrary shear or six-axis wrench, and not every desired contact motion is mechanically realizable.
records.plan_action: Store each taxel's rigid link, local position and unit normal. Construct its link-specific Jacobian; test zero influence of downstream joints. Keep vector force reconstruction outside the baseline specification.
records.novelty: Generalized contact control is prior art; no new control theorem is claimed.

records.title: Human-robot coexistence and contact handling with redundant robots
records.bibliography: E. Magrini and A. De Luca, IROS 2017, pp. 4611–4617; DOI 10.1109/IROS.2017.8206331.
records.read_scope: Author PDF, 7 pages; introduction, §III including Remark 1, §IV handling logic and transition description read.
records.finding: The method changes task behavior across contact-intensity thresholds and interpolates velocity during task abort to reduce jerk. Remark 1 specifies a single-contact algorithm in the reported formulation.
records.limitation: An extension discussion is not experimental proof for arbitrary simultaneous contacts. Gradual stopping trades reduced jerk against additional motion/time.
records.plan_action: Use explicit MONITOR, CONTACT, CONTROLLED_HOLD and FAULT states with hysteresis and latched recovery. Opposing/multiple contacts or infeasible relief request OEM hold rather than ambiguous automatic withdrawal. Test both contact onset and release.
records.novelty: Contact-aware task relaxation/abort is established; robustness and cost evidence are the potential contribution.

records.title: Human body part multicontact recognition and detection methodology
records.bibliography: K. S. Kim and L. Sentis, ICRA 2017, pp. 1908–1915; DOI 10.1109/ICRA.2017.7989222.
records.read_scope: UT Austin author-hosted abstract/introduction via search index. Direct PDF fetch failed; author-uploaded secondary full text found but not substituted for a verified full read.
records.finding: The system combines a 3D time-of-flight scanner with wheel-drivetrain torque sensing to associate contacts with body parts and classify predetermined interaction gestures.
records.limitation: This is sensor fusion with a restricted gesture vocabulary, not proof that normal touch intensity alone reveals arbitrary human intent or body part.
records.plan_action: Expose contact facts separately from application intent. Deliberate teaching/interaction requires explicit enable and allowed zones; any later gesture model must publish confusion matrices including accidental-contact negatives.
records.novelty: Multimodal touch-gesture interpretation is existing research.

records.title: Long-term training with a brain-machine interface-based gait protocol induces partial neurological recovery in paraplegic patients
records.bibliography: A. R. C. Donati et al., Scientific Reports 6, 30383, 2016; DOI 10.1038/srep30383.
records.read_scope: Publisher-indexed abstract and bibliographic identity; publisher full text redirected to an inaccessible identity service and PMC4980986 returned a browser challenge. No methods-section audit claimed.
records.finding: The abstract reports outcomes in eight participants after a year of a combined brain-machine-interface gait-training protocol incorporating multiple feedback/training components.
records.limitation: The abstract does not isolate electronic skin's causal contribution. It does not establish clinical benefit of this proposed skin, nor authorize extrapolation to rehabilitation products.
records.plan_action: Keep medical/rehabilitation claims outside the proof-of-concept article and commercial baseline. Sensory feedback may be mentioned as a distinct future application requiring its own clinical evidence and development program.
records.novelty: Bio-inspired sensory feedback is prior art; this project is initially a robot perception product.
